name: Wang Haijun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Atour Lifestyle Holdings (Nasdaq: ATAT)
profile: Wang Haijun (王海军) founded Atour, China's largest mid-to-upscale hotel chain, in 2012-13 after years at Home Inns, Jinjiang Inn and as EVP of China Lodging (now H World). Atour listed on Nasdaq in 2022 and pairs hotels with a fast-growing sleep-products retail business. He is a Yanshan University graduate with a CEIBS EMBA.
interesting_fact: Atour also runs a large retail arm selling the pillows, bedding and mattresses guests use in its hotels, a key growth driver alongside its hotel network.
deep_cut_fact: Atour is named after Yaduo (亚朵) village in Nujiang, Yunnan: after leaving Hanting in 2012 Wang travelled to Bhutan and Nepal, then found in Yaduo the same simple contentment and named the brand after it. He long used the nickname 耶律胤 (Yelü Yin), a nod to his reported Khitan ancestry.
notes: Hosts quarterly earnings calls in English/Chinese; IR via Christensen Advisory is the most practical route.

name: Cai Rongjun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, OFILM Group (欧菲光, SZSE: 002456)
profile: Cai Rongjun (蔡荣军), born 1972 in rural Jieyang, Guangdong, founded Shenzhen O-film in 2002, a maker of camera modules, touch panels and optical components listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After losing Apple business in 2020, OFILM pivoted to Chinese smartphone makers and automotive optics/smart-car components; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: OFILM was once one of Apple's key camera-module and touch-panel suppliers; after Apple dropped it in 2020 the company rebuilt around Huawei and other Chinese phone brands and in-car camera/lidar modules.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Shantou University in 1995 he worked a few months at a Guangzhou telephone factory, then joined Kodak repairing equipment on a then-princely salary of 10,000+ yuan a month; he has said that if Kodak hadn't declined he might still be working there instead of founding OFILM.
notes: Board secretary Zhou Liang (周亮) is the formal IR contact. Cai earned a DBA from the University of Minnesota in 2024 (per company filings).

name: Angeliki Frangou
current_role: Chairwoman and CEO, Navios Maritime Partners L.P. (NYSE: NMM); head of the Navios Group
profile: Greek shipowner born 1965 in Chios to a family of Kardamyla shipowners. After working as an analyst at Republic National Bank in New York, she started her own shipping business in 1990 and in 2005 took control of Navios Maritime Holdings via a SPAC; she now runs Navios Partners, a diversified dry-bulk, container and tanker owner.
interesting_fact: She acquired Navios in 2005 through a blank-check company (International Shipping Enterprises) that raised about $200m, an early use of a SPAC in shipping; Lloyd's List ranked her 29th in its 2025 list of shipping's 100 most influential people.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a mechanical engineer (BS Fairleigh Dickinson, MS Columbia), was named the Connecticut Maritime Association's Commodore for 2011, and collects Greek, Byzantine and Chinese art and loves opera.
notes: Hosts Navios Partners quarterly earnings calls; speaks at Capital Link and Posidonia shipping forums, which may be a good outreach route.

name: Huang Kangjing
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~74%) of LVGEM (China) Real Estate Investment Co. (HKEX: 0095) and founder of the Shenzhen-based LVGEM Group
profile: Huang Kangjing (黄康境) built LVGEM Group, a Shenzhen developer specialising in urban-village redevelopment, and controls Hong Kong-listed LVGEM (China) Real Estate. He keeps a low public profile; the listed company is chaired by a family member and is best known for the giant Baishizhou urban-renewal project in Nanshan, Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: LVGEM is behind the Baishizhou redevelopment in Shenzhen, once valued by a broker at about RMB 220bn, among the largest urban-village renewal schemes in China; phase 1 ('Baishizhou Jingting') began handover in Feb 2026.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews or personal bio found. Dropped off Hurun after 2023 as LVGEM posted heavy losses. Best route is the company's general contact in Hong Kong.

name: Hua Yong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Shunwang Technology (SZSE: 300113)
profile: Hua Yong (华勇) spent about a decade at the state-owned Hangzhou Telecommunication Bureau before co-founding Shunwang in July 2005 to make internet-cafe management software; it listed on ChiNext in 2010. After stepping back in 2022 he returned as chairman in 2023 and is repurposing Shunwang's internet-cafe network into a distributed edge-computing (GPU cloud) business.
interesting_fact: Shunwang now runs 330+ edge-computing node rooms serving ~820,000 terminals with ~53,000 'channels' of operable GPU compute (Q1 2026), renting cloud gaming/AI PCs to internet cafes - a direct edge data-center angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Shunwang's flagship product was '网维大师' (Wangwei Dashi), maintenance software for internet cafes; Hua has described his return and the pivot of that cafe network into edge-compute nodes as a 'second startup' (二次创业).
notes: Very relevant to data-center/edge compute theme. Board secretary Rong Songyi (戎颂怡) handles investor communications; Shunwang holds regular IR sessions recorded on cninfo.

name: Chen Lifen
current_role: Former chairwoman and general manager, Jiangsu Sunshine Co. (SSE: 600220); long-time executive of Sunshine Group, Jiangyin (current role unclear)
profile: Chen Lifen (陈丽芬) grew up with Jiangyin's Sunshine Group, a fine worsted-wool fabric and suit maker, rising to chair listed Jiangsu Sunshine and steering its move into high-end fabrics, branding and later biomedical and environmental businesses. The parent Sunshine Group entered court-supervised restructuring in March 2025 and she has not appeared on Hurun lists since 2021.
interesting_fact: At its peak Sunshine produced on average 100,000 m of worsted fabric, 10,000 suits and 10,000 shirts a day, and was the first Jiangsu company to win the China Quality Award.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 Sunshine Group took on the international secretariat of ISO's textiles technical committee (ISO/TC38), the first Chinese firm to host an ISO technical committee secretariat; she has said 'Sunshine Group gave me a golden, sunny life' (是阳光集团给了我一个金色的阳光人生).
notes: Sunshine Group is in restructuring (2025) and the listed company has had regulatory issues; Lu Yu chaired Jiangsu Sunshine 2023-2025. Low-priority / sensitive outreach target; no personal or office contact found.

name: Gao Junfang
current_role: None - former chairwoman of Changsheng Bio-technology (delisted); serving a life sentence
profile: Gao Junfang (高俊芳) was chairwoman of Changchun Changsheng Bio-technology, a vaccine maker at the centre of China's 2018 falsified rabies-vaccine scandal. The company was delisted and bankrupt; she was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Changchun Intermediate Court in Jan 2026, upheld on appeal by the Jilin High Court in Sept 2026.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: imprisoned (life sentence, final Sept 2026), fortune confiscated, company defunct. Recommend removing from the list.

name: Hsin Chung-Herng
current_role: Chairman, Taiwan Union Technology Corp. (TUC, 台燿科技, TPEx: 6274)
profile: Hsin Chung-Herng (辛忠衡; the input's 辛忠卫 appears to be a typo) chairs Taiwan Union Technology, a Taiwanese maker of copper-clad laminates and prepregs for printed circuit boards. Demand for its high-speed, low-loss laminates in AI servers and data-center switches has driven a surge in its share price, putting him on the Hurun list in 2026.
interesting_fact: TUC began in 1974 as Taiwan Union Glass, an optical-glass maker, and only switched to copper-clad laminates in 1997; its 'ThunderClad' low-loss materials are now used in AI server and high-speed networking boards.
notes: Strong AI/data-center supply-chain angle. Very low public profile; no interviews found. Company spokesperson listed as Huang Wen-hsu (黄文旭) per TechNews company data (https://info.technews.tw/company/04226091-台燿科技股份有限公司); TUC held a 2026 AGM with director elections, so confirm chair post-AGM.

name: He Jinbi
current_role: None - founder and former chairman of Maike Metals International (Xi'an), now bankrupt; sentenced to life imprisonment (appeal reported)
profile: He Jinbi (何金碧), born 1964 in Xi'an, co-founded Maike in 1993 with a RMB 50,000 loan and built it into a trader handling roughly a quarter of China's refined copper imports. Maike hit a liquidity crisis in 2022, went bankrupt, and a Xi'an court sentenced He to life for contract fraud and bribery (reported 2026).
notes: Not a viable outreach target: detained since 2023, life sentence for fraud, company bankrupt (co-listed with Zhang Chunling). Recommend removing from the list.

name: Yan Deping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hefei Hengxin Life Science & Technology (恒鑫生活, SZSE ChiNext: 301501)
profile: Yan Deping (严德平) left a teaching job in 1997 to start a small commercial print shop in Hefei, then pivoted around 2000 into paper cups and later biodegradable (PLA) food-service ware. Hengxin now supplies cups and packaging to tea and coffee chains such as Luckin and Mixue, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Hengxin is a national 'little giant' specialist in biodegradable tableware, with annual capacity of around 9 billion cups and containers serving China's booming tea-and-coffee chains.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 11 years as a teacher at Hefei Forestry Vocational & Technical School; at 34 he started 'Hengxin Printing' with second-hand presses, doing design, printing and sales himself, and the paper know-how led him into paper cups.
notes: Hurun lists the company as 'HXIN'. Co-founded with spouse Fan Yanru. Company holds online investor Q&A sessions (e.g. 15 May 2026).

name: Guo Xinping
current_role: Largest individual shareholder (22.21%) of Beijing UniStrong Science & Technology (合众思壮, SZSE: 002383); not the controlling shareholder since a Zhengzhou state-owned investor took control (c. 2019)
profile: A Guo Xinping (郭信平) founded Beijing UniStrong, a satellite-navigation (GPS/BeiDou) and high-precision positioning company that listed in Shenzhen in 2010, matching his Hurun appearances from 2010. Control later passed to a Zhengzhou Airport Economy Zone state entity; he still held 22.21% at end-2025.
interesting_fact: UniStrong was an early Chinese maker of handheld GPS receivers and later moved into BeiDou-based high-precision positioning for surveying, agriculture and mapping.
notes: Identity not fully confirmed: input lists source of wealth as 'Yibei' / financial software, but filings tie Guo Xinping to UniStrong (GNSS). His UniStrong shares are recorded as frozen (2025 annual report) - sensitive. Web-search budget ran out before this could be resolved.

name: David Richwhite
current_role: Private investor; co-founder of Fay, Richwhite & Company (retired from active banking)
profile: New Zealand investment banker (b. 1948) who co-founded merchant bank Fay Richwhite with Sir Michael Fay in 1973. The firm advised on and co-invested in NZ privatisations (Bank of New Zealand, Telecom NZ, NZ Rail) and backed the consortium that formed UK rail-freight operator EWS. Based in Geneva 1998-2003, he now lives in London.
interesting_fact: With Michael Fay he bankrolled New Zealand's first three America's Cup challenges (1987, 1988 'Big Boat' KZ1, 1992), and they later gifted KZ1 to Auckland's maritime museum.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 Fay and Richwhite took a team to San Francisco and won the One Ton Cup with the Bruce Farr-designed yacht 'Propaganda' (KZ 6161); he also co-owns Great Mercury Island off the Coromandel with Fay.
notes: Very private; no public office, website or social accounts found. Rail-freight and privatisation history may be a hook. Avoid the Winebox Inquiry topic.

name: Zhu Baoliang
current_role: Head of Honglou Group (红楼集团, Hangzhou); with family/Honglou the controlling shareholder group of Lishang Guochao (丽尚国潮, SSE: 600738, formerly Lanzhou Minbai)
profile: Zhu Baoliang (朱宝良) built Hangzhou-based Honglou Group, which spans department stores and retail, real estate and investment. Through Honglou he acquired control of Lanzhou Minbai (now Lishang Guochao), a Lanzhou department-store operator, folding in Honglou retail assets in a 2017 restructuring.
interesting_fact: The listed company was renamed from Lanzhou Minbai to Lishang Guochao ('China-chic'), refocusing on domestic 'guochao' consumer brands alongside its legacy department stores.
notes: Co-listed with Hong Yidan (spouse). Low public profile; web-search budget exhausted, so personal background was not researched further. 2025 annual report shows his directly held shares as frozen - sensitive.
